tone_statements.quote: Limi has four contrastive tones on monosyllabic words, all in modal phonationː rising [²⁴], mid [³³], high [⁵⁵], and low [²¹]. … In disyllabic words, all possible tone combinations are found … only syllables with initial sonorants show the full tonal inventory, due to the conditioning of the Limi Tone 1 split: syllables with voiced initials developed the rising tone, whereas elsewhere Tone 1 is now a mid level tone. … The low tone [21] is realized with a falling contour, which may be an automatic transition to the lowest pitch level rather than phonemic contour

tone.quote: Limi has four contrastive tones on monosyllabic words, all in modal phonationː rising [²⁴], mid [³³], high [⁵⁵], and low [²¹]. … In disyllabic words, all possible tone combinations are found … only syllables with initial sonorants show the full tonal inventory, due to the conditioning of the Limi Tone 1 split: syllables with voiced initials developed the rising tone, whereas elsewhere Tone 1 is now a mid level tone. … The low tone [21] is realized with a falling contour, which may be an automatic transition to the lowest pitch level rather than phonemic contour
tone.says: Four contrastive tones on every syllable: rising 24, mid 33, high 55, low 21 (the rising tone split from Tone 1 after voiced initials); only allotonic sandhi; Praat F0 study of two speakers.

sources.note: Appendix 3, the Ngwi comparative tone box, gives for every Proto-Ngwi tone category (*1, *2, *3, checked *H, *L) crossed with proto-initial class the modern tone value in each lect. Yongde Limi column: four values -- 24 (rising) for *1 with voiced/nasal/approximant initials, 33 for *1 with voiceless or glottal/s-prefixed initials and for all of *3 and most of *H, 21 for *2 with plain initials and for *L with voiced/plain initials, 55 for *2 and *L with glottal-stop/s- prefixed initials (a few *H cells '33, 55').
